purpose: Overlay Wave 9 linked hot-runner/melt-control quality evidence onto the Book chapter coverage map while preserving the raw synchronized actuator-state dataset gap.

overlays.newEditorialCapability: Teach a direct evidence chain from distributed/local melt-valve action through pressure/flow control to measured dimensions, part-weight consistency, process capability and productivity trade-offs.
overlays.boundary: All four sources belong to one broader research family and use legacy dynamic/self-regulating valve architectures; they are not four independent replications and do not substitute for modern raw servo-state traces.

overlays.newEditorialCapability: Show that cavity balance is not only a fill or pressure concept: local melt-delivery control can alter dimensional consistency, knit-line position and cavity-specific production flexibility.
Add controlled examples where process capability and short-term quality variation changed after local melt-pressure control, while keeping every numerical gain tied to its experimental system.
Link local melt-pressure/shrinkage control to multiple measured dimensions rather than treating dimensional variation solely as a global machine-setting problem.

Use a case-specific example showing that local melt-pressure control can interact with clamp-tonnage and cycle-time requirements; do not convert reported reductions into generic clamp-sizing guidance.

wantedChannels: commanded valve state or target position
remainingTargetedRawDataGap.note: Wave 9 materially strengthens the causal teaching narrative but adds no public synchronized raw dataset containing all required channels.
